words.gloss: that which is to be avoided

literal: That which is to be done, examining, is virtue alone for one; that which is to be escaped, examining, is blame.
translation: If one examines what a person ought to do, it is virtue alone; if one examines what must be avoided, it is vice.
modern: ஒருவன் தன் வாழ்வில் செய்யத் தகுந்தது அறம் மட்டுமே; அவன் தப்பித்துத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டியது பழி தரும் செயல்களே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the fundamental choice in human action. The word 'ceyal' refers to doing, while 'uyal' refers to escaping or avoiding; both are joined with 'palatu' to mean 'that which is of the nature of'. The repeated word 'orum' implies that careful examination will always lead to this conclusion. By using the emphatic suffix 'e' in 'arane', the text stresses that virtue is the only true course of action, dividing all deeds simply into virtue to be practiced and blame to be shunned.
